tagline.text: A hands-on farm park in the Tagaytay highlands where you feed the animals

location.label: Location
location.text: Maglabe Drive, Km. 63 Panungyan, Mendez, Cavite

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,500 (per person, including admission, activities and meals)

children.text: This theme farm of roughly 10–12 hectares sits in the highlands of Mendez, Cavite. Families feed farm animals such as llamas, miniature horses, rabbits and ducks, then stroll the gardens and the honey bee farm. It pairs easily with a trip to Tagaytay.

Paradizoo is a theme farm in the Panungyan area of Mendez, Cavite, more precisely where Maglabe Drive branches off the Mendez–Tagaytay Road. Its address reads Km. 63, Panungyan, Mendez, Cavite, and it is run by Zoomanity Group, a Philippine animal theme park operator. The same group also runs Zoobic Safari in Subic and Zoori in Tagaytay, but Paradizoo is not a conventional zoo with tigers or crocodiles. Think of it as a farm and garden with animal experiences added.

Sources describe the grounds as 10–12 hectares, which feels quite large when you walk it slowly. Instead of tigers, monkeys or crocodiles, it is described as having domestic and farm-raised animals such as llamas, camels, miniature horses and ostriches, while smaller animals such as ducks, geese, rabbits, sheep, donkeys, goats, turtles and parakeets can be fed by hand. With vegetable, flower and meditation gardens, an orchid pavilion, a honey bee farm and a butterfly farm, it is also a pleasant place for adults who are not especially keen on animals.
Mendez sits at an elevation of about

, so it is cooler than Manila and fairly comfortable even at midday. Some stretches have little shade, though, so bring a hat and sunscreen. It works as a day trip from Manila, and many visitors combine it with the viewpoints and cafes of nearby Tagaytay.

Admission prices have varied a lot by period and ticket type. The sources I found list adult entry at ₱199 in a 2018 blog, ₱249 in an article dated November 2024, and ₱399 (including a ₱200 voucher) for the day-tour ticket in a late-2023 review, so they do not agree. Treat every price in this guide as approximate and check the latest rates with the official channels or a booking site before you go.

Feed animals such as rabbits, ducks, geese, sheep, miniature horses and donkeys. Feed is often sold as a separate set from the admission ticket and contains grass, carrots and seeds. Sheep, horses and donkeys are fed from outside the pen.

The park is described as having llamas, camels, ostriches and miniature horses, animals rarely seen in ordinary zoos. The mix of animals and whether camel or horse rides are offered can change over time, so check at the entrance.

Flower, vegetable, meditation and eclectic gardens run one into the next, making a pleasant walk with plenty of photo spots. The vegetable garden is described as using methods such as worm compost and hydroponics, and there is a corner where you can pick produce and buy it to take home.

blocks.title: Honey bee farm and butterfly garden

children.text: The honey bee farm explains bee life and how honey is made, and the butterfly garden lets you see butterflies up close. Reviews mention a small separate fee for both, so confirm on site.
Orchid and bromeliad pavilions suit visitors who like plants. When the flowers peak varies from year to year, so it helps to look at the official social media photos before you visit.

blocks.title: Archery, bubble ball and other activities

children.text: Activities described include archery with an instructor who teaches the stance and a bubble ball you roll around the field. Many are aimed at children, so check age and height limits on site.
Many children spend a long time watching turtles swim or come out of their shells, and the parakeets may fly to your hand if you hold out seeds. If you have kids, expect to spend a lot of time here.

Cottages such as log cabins, A-frame houses and tiny houses are described in a quiet wooded part of the farm. Rates and inclusions change over time, so check the official information. Staying overnight lets you enjoy the farm in the quiet morning hours.

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: A farm day trip from Manila

children.text: Leave Manila and head toward Tagaytay, which takes about
2–3 hours
. Roads clog on weekends and holidays, so it is best to leave early.
Turn onto Maglabe Drive from the Mendez–Tagaytay Road and arrive at Paradizoo. Buy your tickets at the entrance, and if you plan to feed the animals, buy a feed set too.
Feed the rabbits, ducks, geese and goats in the animal area. If you have children, take your time at the turtle pond and the parakeet area.
Grab a light meal at the cafe on the farm or rest at a picnic spot such as the meditation garden. Check the rules on outside food on site.
Walk slowly through the flower and vegetable gardens, the honey bee farm and the orchid pavilion. Some facilities may close early in the afternoon, so see the ones you care about first.
Stop by the souvenir shop, then head toward Tagaytay for coffee at a cafe with a view.
Some booking sites list the last admission as 3:00 PM. If you arrive late, some facilities may be closed, so we recommend entering early.

items.title: Two-day plan
items.subtitle: A farm stay combined with Tagaytay

children.text: Arrive and enter, look around the gardens and animal areas, then drop your bags at the cottage.
Stroll in the late afternoon when the farm quiets down, and try archery or a garden activity.
Have dinner at your cottage or at a nearby restaurant in Tagaytay. Check at booking whether dinner is available on the farm.
The next morning, have the breakfast made with farm vegetables if your stay includes it, then revisit the animal area during the quiet hours before the park fills up.
After checkout, head to People's Park in the Sky in Tagaytay or a viewpoint cafe.

items.title: From Manila by car or taxi

children.text: Take the road from Manila toward Tagaytay, then look for Maglabe Drive off the Mendez–Tagaytay Road. Depending on traffic, the trip can take
2–3 hours
or more.
Typing Paradizoo into Google Maps gives you directions, but the farm lies back from the main road, so take care not to miss the Maglabe Drive turn.
We could not confirm whether private-car parking is available or what it costs, so check on site.
Ride-hailing services such as Grab may struggle to find a return car from the edge of Mendez, so consider negotiating a round-trip charter fare in advance.
Take a Tagaytay-bound bus from a terminal in Manila such as Pasay or Cubao. Exact boarding points and routes change over time, so check the latest information.
Transfer at Tagaytay or the Olivarez terminal to a Mendez-bound jeepney or bus, and ask to be let off at Maglabe Drive.
From Maglabe Drive to the farm entrance, take a tricycle.
Published material says a shuttle once ran to Paradizoo from the Zoori side on the Tagaytay–Nasugbu Road. Whether it runs now, and when, needs to be confirmed.
Within Tagaytay, a taxi or ride-hailing car is the simplest way to get there.

It is open all year, but because the gardens and animal activities are outdoors, the dry season is more comfortable. Being in the highlands it is cooler than Manila, but in the rainy season paths get wet and some outdoor activities may be limited.
Weekday mornings are relatively quiet. On weekends, holidays and school breaks, group tours and families increase and lines can grow, so arrive early.

The farm has accommodation introduced under the name Banig and Breakfast. It comes in forms such as log cabins, A-frame houses and tiny houses, and is said to include breakfast made with farm vegetables and admission tickets. Rates and packages may have changed over time, so check through official channels.
You can eat simply at the Paradizoo cafe on the farm, and menus using farm vegetables have been featured. For a proper meal, nightlife or a cafe tour, the nearby town of Tagaytay is more convenient.
Arrive early. One reviewer arrived close to 5:00 PM and found that some facilities had already closed.
If you plan to feed the animals, buy a feed set when you enter. For children it is often the highlight.
Bring non-slip shoes, a hat, sunscreen and water. You will walk a lot on garden paths and dirt tracks.
Discount vouchers on booking sites (such as Klook) or in apps are sometimes cheaper than the ticket window, so compare before you leave.
To combine it with Tagaytay, do the farm in the morning and the viewpoints and cafes in the afternoon.
Wash your hands after touching the animals, and do not let children eat with hands that have touched them.
In some areas staff take family photos, and prints and souvenirs may cost extra.
We could not confirm entry rules, whether pets are allowed, or whether outside food may be brought in, so ask the official contacts before you go.
Admission and some activity and lodging prices differed between sources, so check the latest information with the official channels or a booking site before you visit.
When feeding animals, follow staff instructions and do not put your face close or stick out your fingers.
Do not enter the pens, and feed sheep, horses and donkeys from outside the pen.
Keep children with an adult at all times. There are ponds and water features.
The last admission time and the closing of some facilities can be earlier than the stated opening hours.
Highland weather can turn rainy suddenly, so bring an umbrella in the wet season.
A highland resort about
20–30 minutes
by car, with cafes overlooking the volcano lake and markets. It can take longer depending on traffic.
A viewpoint park on the Tagaytay ridge with a sweeping view of Taal Lake and the volcano.
A Spanish colonial-era town in Batangas; it is better to plan it as a day or more combined with Paradizoo.
A zoo in Tagaytay run by the same group. Admission has sometimes been included with a stay, but the current terms need to be confirmed.
